body: ADDITIONAL P1 ON THE SAME EXACT REVIEW — platform-specific downstream consumers of a changed SHARED declaration are invisible. The exit-4 preflight inspects only changed paths, while consumer search scans module/src and module/.jvm/src only. Independent court: baseline core shared SharedPlatformApi plus its only downstream consumer at features/.js/src/test/scala/JsConsumer.scala; candidate modifies only the shared API. Exact 609e35f script exits 0, lists only core, and emits coreJVM/test. It neither names features nor refuses the incomplete platform scope. This is distinct from a changed .js path: the consumer survives unchanged and is precisely what a reference-scope tool must discover. Required successor must search .js and .native consumer roots for every changed type; since this script emits JVM tasks only, either fail 4 and name those consumer paths/modules, or implement exact JS/Native tasks plus courts. Add shared-change-with-JS-only-consumer and Native symmetry courts. This amends my prior “no other finding”; modifier recognition and platform-consumer discovery are both blocking.
